builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
summary: The method replaces manual 3D asset authoring and single-pass LLM 3D code generation with a multi-agent DAG harness that iteratively generates, executes, measures, and visually verifies executable 3D programs, plus a 2M-sample dataset for fine-tuning open models. Costs include repeated model and rendering calls per asset (raising API spend and latency), infrastructure to execute untrusted 3D code with its declared environments and assets, and fine-tuning compute if the dataset is used. It can fail where execution environments are brittle or unavailable, where automated visual and spatial checks misjudge aesthetic or semantic quality, and the 90% win-rate claim covers one competitor and one backing model, so it may not transfer to other stacks or asset categories.
rationale: The harness pattern and open dataset are usable with API models or locally fine-tuned small open models, but the quality gains are demonstrated only for 3D content tasks and must be validated against the reader's actual asset requirements before production adoption.
technique: Multi-agent 3D code generation with execution-based verification

claims.statement: The method replaces manual 3D asset authoring and single-pass LLM 3D code generation with a multi-agent DAG harness that iteratively generates, executes, measures, and visually verifies executable 3D programs, plus a 2M-sample dataset for fine-tuning open models. Costs include repeated model and rendering calls per asset (raising API spend and latency), infrastructure to execute untrusted 3D code with its declared environments and assets, and fine-tuning compute if the dataset is used. It can fail where execution environments are brittle or unavailable, where automated visual and spatial checks misjudge aesthetic or semantic quality, and the 90% win-rate claim covers one competitor and one backing model, so it may not transfer to other stacks or asset categories.

The 3DCodeVerse harness achieves a 90% win rate against Claude Design (3D Object) in pairwise human evaluations when both are driven by Claude Opus 5.5; fine-tuning open models on the 2M-program dataset is reported to significantly improve 3D coding ability, without a stated multiplicative factor.
